To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SEIRAS technique is a powerful tool to monitor the orientational behavior of molecules during their adsorption to the surface and that the biotinylation of the cysteamine layer leads to an ordered biotin layer that interacts with streptavidin with high specificity.

(i) the SEIRAS technique allows for monitoring the individual assembling steps of membrane proteins in situ on the molecular level, and (ii) the streptavidins/biotin inter-layer is superior to the His-tag/NiTAA inter-layer in the regeneration of membrane proteins.
the biotinylation of cysteamine layers yields densely packed layers and that streptavidin binding to these layers is highly specific.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new interlayer for the immobilisation of strep-tag proteins on gold surfaces.
the orientated assembly and immobilization of membrane proteins on a gold surface by means of a streptavidine/biotin inter-layer.
the orientated assembly on the molecular level of streptavidinated biotin and strep-tagged proteins on the gold electrode surface by SEIRAS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the strep-tag/biotin/streptavidin system provides a promising alternative to the well established His-tag/NiNTA system for orientated assembly of membrane proteins on the surface.
the streptavidinstrep-tag system is superior to the His-tag/NtA system with respect to the orientated assembly and regeneration of membrane proteins on the Au surface.
the strep-tag/biotin/streptavidin interlayer is a suitable interlayer for orientated immobilization of membrane proteins on the molecular level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SEIRAS allows us to track the individual assembly steps and to identify the bottlenecks in the process of the orientated protein assembly.

the biotinylation of cysteamine self-assembled monalayer and subsequent adsorption of strep-tag on the streptavidi/biotin interayer is a suitable strategy for orientated assembling of the strep tag membrane protein on a solid support.
SEIRAS is an excellent tool for in situ monitoring of the assembly process of strep-tag proteins on the molecular level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SEIRA can be used as a powerful tool for monitoring and optimizing surface modification steps for the orientated assembly and immobilization of membrane proteins on gold surfaces.
the SEIRA spectroscopic approach can serve to characterize the assembly of membrane proteins on a solid substrate.
the SEIRA technique is a powerful tool to monitor the orientating assembly of membrane proteins on the molecular level.
